title: Showing percentages in Excel

primary_objective.statement: Predict what a cell shows after Percentage format is applied, and store percent results as decimals.

sources.title: Format numbers as percentages in Excel
Prealgebra 2e
sources.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; publisher prohibits use for training large language models

teach.text: In Excel, a number format changes how a value looks, not the value stored in the cell. The Percentage format shows the stored value multiplied by 100, followed by a % sign.

So a cell that stores 0.25 shows 25%. A cell that already stores 25 shows 2500%. For percent results, keep the value as a decimal, then apply Percentage format. You can apply it with the Percent Style button on the Home tab.
A percent-change formula such as =(B2-A2)/A2 gives a decimal, like 0.25. Percentage format then shows it as 25%. The number of decimal places you choose rounds what you see, not the stored value.

examples.text: A cell stores 0.3. With Percentage format it shows 30%, because 0.3 × 100 = 30.
A2 holds 80 and B2 holds 100. =(B2-A2)/A2 gives (100 − 80) ÷ 80 = 0.25. With Percentage format the cell shows 25%.

alternate_explanations.text: Think of Percentage format as a pair of glasses. The cell still holds 0.25, but through the glasses you see it × 100 with a % sign: 25%. Take the glasses off (General format) and you see 0.25 again.

checks.prompt: A cell stores 0.07. You apply Percentage format with 0 decimal places. What does the cell show?
A cell already stores the number 12. You apply Percentage format with 0 decimal places. What does the cell show?
checks.feedback: Percentage format shows the stored value × 100, so 12 appears as 1200%. To show 12%, store 0.12 instead.

checks.prompt: A2 holds 50 and B2 holds 65. C2 contains =(B2-A2)/A2 with Percentage format and 0 decimal places. What number appears before the % sign?
checks.feedback: (65 − 50) ÷ 50 = 0.3. Percentage format shows 0.3 × 100 = 30, so C2 shows 30%.

return_cue: Back to your spreadsheet: let the formula produce a decimal, then apply Percentage format to show it as a percent.
